target.title: feat(heartbeat): add config to preserve silent task results in agent context
target.body: Closes #95811 ## What Problem This Solves The `agents.defaults.heartbeat.ackMaxChars` config affected two unrelated behaviors: * Delivering a message to the user * Building the message history for the bot context These behaviors should be configurable separately. This PR adds a new config field to decouple the behavior. Concretely, this allows users to avoid being notified when the bot completes a heartbeat task while still allowing the bot to retain what it did during that task in memory. ## Why This Change Was Made This adds a config-gated heartbeat transcript mode that preserves the existing default behavior, while allowing users to keep only the final heartbeat result in future model context. Heartbeat poll prompts, tool calls, and tool results remain stripped in that mode, so background tasks can be remembered without notifying the user or bloating replay history. ## User Impact Users can run silent heartbeat tasks that produce useful results without being notified immediately, while still letting the agent remember those results for later follow-up. Existing heartbeat behavior remains unchanged by default. ## Evidence This is after the PR. Before the PR, the bot would just answer that it cannot see any heartbeat task in the history. (Note: Specifically because it ends the task with HEARTBEAT_OK, but this is what I want - the bot compile interesting stuff and only tell me about it if I ask. I don't want it to message me after each run.) Image description: > User message: Was there any interesting result in your heartbeat task from 3 hours ago? > Bot message: Yeah! target.title: fix(agents): use CJK-aware token estimation for tool results
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2` 与 `estimateStringChars`的中文字符权重(4 chars/token)不匹配，导致CJK-rich内容被2倍高估，触发false token overflow错误，中断中文工作流。

例如：85k中文字符被估计为170k tokens，实际应为~85k，导致本不应触发的preemptive compaction提前激活。

## Evidence
### Verifiable Behavior
- **Issue Reference**: #95327
- **Test Results**:
```
[pnpm test] preemptive-compaction.test.ts
Tests 21 passed (21)
Duration 6.03s

CJK Text Test: 85,000+ Chinese chars estimated as ~85,000 tokens (ratio: ~1.0)
CJK Tool Result Test: 80k CJK chars fit within 128k budget with 20k reserve
Mixed Lang Test: ratio 0.8-1.5, healthy
JSON Payload Test: CJK-heavy JSON tool result no longer triggers false overflow
Non-serializable Test: circular non-array content completes precheck without throwing
```

### Real Behavior Proof
Below is the terminal output from running a standalone script against this PR branch. The script exercises the actual production estimation helpers (`estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure` and `shouldPreemptivelyCompactBeforePrompt`) with realistic CJK-heavy, mixed, and Latin-only tool-result payloads.

The output below was generated by a temporary local script that imports the production `estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure` and `shouldPreemptivelyCompactBeforePrompt` helpers and exercises them with the payloads shown above.

```
=== PR #95447 real-behavior proof: CJK-aware tool-result token estimation ===

--- 85k CJK-heavy tool result ---
  Input chars:              85,000
  CJK ratio:                90.0%
  Adjusted char weight:     314,500 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 165,173  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  94,421  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          fits
  After-fix overflow:       0 tokens

--- Mixed CJK + Latin tool result (CJK majority) ---
  Input chars:              49,000
  CJK ratio:                61.2%
  Adjusted char weight:     139,000 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 73,035  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  41,771  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          fits
  After-fix overflow:       0 tokens

--- Latin-only tool result ---
  Input chars:              67,000
  CJK ratio:                0.0%
  Adjusted char weight:     67,000 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 35,235  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  40,271  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          compact_then_truncate
  After-fix overflow:       13,271 tokens

=== Result ===
CJK-heavy tool results no longer trigger false overflow;
non-CJK tool results keep the existing conservative estimate.
```

The proof shows that a 85k-character CJK-heavy tool result was previously estimated at ~165k tokens (false overflow → would route to `compact_only`) and is now estimated at ~94k tokens (fits within a 128k budget with 20k reserve → routes to `fits`). The Latin-only case still uses the conservative `/2` ratio and correctly routes to compaction when it genuinely overflows.

### Technical Evidence
- **Before**: `TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2` 导致CJK被double-count
- **After**:
  - CJK比例≥50%时使用`ESTIMATED_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4`，与正常文本估计一致
  - 非CJK场景保持保守`/2`比例
  - JSON tool-result payload 和 unknown record fallback 现在也被纳入 CJK ratio 采样
  - ratio pre-pass 使用与 token-pressure 估算相同的 `safeJsonStringify` fallback，避免非序列化内容抛出
- **Files Changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.ts`
  - `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
- **Test Updates**: `preemptive-compaction.test.ts` 增加 5 个 CJK/JSON/fallback 相关测试用例

### Regression Risk
- Low: 仅修改 tool-result token 估算路径，非 CJK 场景保持原有保守行为
- 所有 21 个估计测试通过
- 新增非序列化内容回归测试，确保 precheck 不会因 `JSON.stringify` 失败而中断 turn

## Why This Change Was Made
使 tool result token estimation 与 CJK 字符权重对齐，防止 false overflow，确保多语言工作流公平对待 CJK 字符；同时覆盖 JSON/unknown payload 和安全 fallback，避免 estimator 分支遗漏。

## User Impact
- 中文工作流不再因错误的 token overflow 中断
- Tool result 上下文预算更准确（含结构化 JSON 返回）
- 无配置或操作变更，零用户学习成本

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): harden bridge imports under concurrent syncs
target.body:
## Summary

- Add bounded retry handling for transient `FsSafeError: path-mismatch` while writing imported memory-wiki source pages.
- Coalesce concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same resolved vault/config so `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace` share the same in-flight bridge sync instead of launching duplicate import/index-refresh passes.
- Preserve existing vault safety boundaries for symlink/path-alias and directory-collision cases.
- Rebase the existing PR onto current `origin/main` and keep main's shared guarded page-write path while retaining this PR's imported-source retry and bridge sync coalescing.
- **What did NOT change:** Out of scope and unchanged: no channel delivery, provider routing, plugin-hook contract, gateway method signature, config schema/default, or broad session model change; the behavior change is only the `extensions/memory-wiki` imported-source retry/coalescing path.
- Why it matters / User impact: concurrent memory-wiki bridge imports no longer duplicate expensive import passes or fail the bridge surface on transient filesystem `path-mismatch` races, without weakening path safety.

Related to #91154.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bridge-mode memory-wiki imported-source sync runs through the real OpenClaw gateway surface for `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import`; concurrent bridge calls for the same vault/config coalesce to one underlying bridge ingest/index-refresh pass; transient source-page rewrite pressure does not break the gateway or leave the bridge vault inconsistent.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux worktree `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-91828`, exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422`, local `origin/main` ref `6638a575d39dee5e64ecb562695b70affca8f4b4` during the gateway proof. A post-proof daily-fix drift check against `origin/main` `48e8965b1060d61beda1a52d572373a409317498` found no overlapping changed files and `sync_main_required=false`. Runtime used an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway at `/tmp/openclaw-pr91828-runtime-20260703-proof` with `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and a public `MEMORY.md` artifact in the isolated workspace. Secrets and gateway tokens are not included in the evidence or this PR body.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-91828-evidence/run-gateway-proof-20260703.mjs"
```

The runner starts an exact-head loopback gateway, calls `wiki.status`, `health`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace`, then launches six concurrent gateway calls (`2 x wiki.status`, `2 x wiki.importInsights`, `2 x wiki.palace`), runs eight `wiki.bridge.import` calls while an external writer repeatedly replaces the generated bridge source page, searches the isolated runtime logs for `path-mismatch`/`FsSafeError`/refusal signals, and finally checks that an unknown-method request fails without destabilizing a follow-up `wiki.status`.

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 [P1] exact-head real behavior proof for bridge gateway methods and retry/coalescing behavior:** Addressed for the real gateway surface on exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422`. `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import` all succeeded against bridge mode with a real public memory artifact; the concurrent six-call probe produced exactly one new ingest entry. Remaining gap: the live rewrite-pressure probe did not naturally surface a `path-mismatch` log/error signal, so that part is disclosed instead of overstated.
- **RF-002 [P1] live/local bridge proof gap:** Addressed with an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, memory-core + memory-wiki loaded, `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and `bridgePublicArtifactCount=1` from an actual workspace `MEMORY.md` artifact.
- **RF-003 [P1] session-state / coalescing identity risk:** Addressed by the implementation and runtime probe. The coalescing key includes vault path/mode, bridge/ingest/render/search/context/obsidian config, and agent default/list workspace identity; the runtime concurrent batch updated the live artifact once and produced a single ingest delta across six gateway calls.
- **RF-004 [P1] stale gateway-load / reporter-scale proof:** Partially addressed and partially disclosed. This update supplies exact-head local gateway proof and fresh focused Vitest results after the rebase/conflict resolution; it does not claim the reporter's ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload was rerun.
- **RF-005 [maintainer decision] merge-risk / canonical retry acceptance:** Still requires maintainer judgment. This rebase keeps current main's shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing; maintainers should make the final broad-vs-narrow canonical merge decision.
- **RF-006 [signal] fresh proof / re-review:** This update replaces stale pre-rebase proof with current-head runtime gateway evidence and records it through the daily-fix verification marker. Remaining proof gaps are explicitly listed in `What was not tested` rather than hidden behind local tests.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- ClawSweeper previously flagged overlap with #94443 on transient `path-mismatch` retry behavior.
- This conflict resolution uses the current main shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` retry behavior for the guarded write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing.
- This avoids restoring a divergent direct write retry path, but it does not override the remaining maintainer choice about broad-vs-narrow canonical merge direction.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts`.

- **Command:**

```bash

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts \

```

- **Result:** `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 22 passed (22)` in `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-91828-evidence/focused-vitest-after-sync.log`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** these tests and the runtime gateway proof exercise the memory-wiki import/sync owner boundary that calls `syncImportedSourcesIfNeeded`; they avoid coupling the guardrail to unrelated channel delivery, provider routing, or UI behavior.

## Origin / follow-up

Existing PR tied to #91154. This update rebases the existing PR, resolves the source-page conflict, and revalidates exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422` through the local gateway surface. After proof, daily-fix rechecked drift against `origin/main` ref `48e8965b1060d61beda1a52d572373a409317498`; there were no overlapping changed files and no sync-main requirement.

- **Risk explanation:** Behavior change is limited to memory-wiki import/sync coalescing and imported source-page retry; concurrent callers now share one underlying bridge import/index-refresh pass for the same resolved config identity.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is confined to `extensions/memory-wiki`, coalescing identity includes the bridge artifact-discovery inputs that can change imported source results, and the runtime gateway proof shows repeated/concurrent bridge calls produce one consistent bridge source page and no warnings. Existing symlink/path-alias safety remains outside the retry path.
- **Remaining maintainer decision:** Accept whether this focused imported-source retry/coalescing patch is the desired canonical merge path alongside the broader guarded write behavior already present on main.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same vault/config each performed independent artifact-discovery + import/index-refresh passes, and imported source-page stat/read/write treated transient fs-safe `path-mismatch` races as fatal.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix coalesces at the import/sync source boundary, where bridge artifact discovery and index refresh are owned, and adds bounded retry only for the identified transient filesystem condition rather than masking downstream failures or weakening path safety.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- **Patch quality notes:** No skipped-test or lint suppression claims; no broad refactor. The catch/default paths are narrow guard behavior: `path-mismatch` is rethrown into the bounded retry loop, `not-found`/race reads are treated as no preservable existing notes, and the actual write remains guarded by `writeGuardedVaultPage`, so symlink/path-alias safety is not masked.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #24196.

Discord API allows up to 10 file attachments per message, but the integration only supported a single `mediaUrl`.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `mediaUrls?: string[]` to `DiscordSendOpts`. Auto-batches >10 files across multiple messages. Reply reference only on first batch.
2. **sendDiscordMedia** (`send.shared.ts`): Accepts `mediaUrls: string[]` — iterates all URLs into a single `files` array for Discord's multipart upload.
3. **outbound-payload.ts**: Multiple media URLs batch into one `sendMessageDiscord` call. Component messages reject multiple attachments with a clear error.
4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.
5. **Tests**: 57/57 pass. Coverage for 3-file batch, >10 auto-split with replyTo behavior, legacy backward compatibility.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(discord): add configurable REST API timeout via channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs` to the Discord channel config schema (max 120000ms). Threads it through to `RequestClient` where the REST timeout was previously hardcoded at 15s.

## Root Cause

Large guild operations (ban lists, channel enumeration) and rate-limited endpoints can exceed the 15s default, causing premature `AbortError` failures. The timeout was hardcoded in `extensions/discord/src/internal/rest.ts` with no config override.

## Changes

- `src/config/types.discord.ts`: add `apiTimeoutMs` type (max 120000ms)
- `src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts`: add `apiTimeoutMs` to `DiscordAccountSchema`
- `extensions/discord/src/client.ts`: thread config through `resolveRest()` → `createDiscordRequestClient()`

## Config

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "discord": {
      "apiTimeoutMs": 20000
    }
  }
}
```

Default remains 15000ms for full backward compatibility.

## Testing

- [ ] Config validation: verify `apiTimeoutMs` values from 1-120000 are accepted
- [ ] Config validation: verify out-of-range values are rejected
- [ ] Functional: increase timeout, verify large guild operations no longer hit AbortError
- [ ] Backward compatibility: verify default 15s timeout when `apiTimeoutMs` is not set

target.title: feat: cute GTK-native Linux App (#75)
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: - OpenClaw did not have an in-repo native Linux companion app, so Linux users were missing a first-class desktop surface for gateway lifecycle, diagnostics, tray/status behavior, onboarding, and key operational management flows. - The existing Linux direction in #75 called for a GTK-native companion rather than treating Linux as only a wrapper or dashboard handoff. - Why it matters: - Linux is a real target platform in the issue, and the lack of a native companion left users without parity on core desktop workflows such as service state visibility, tray/status integration, local diagnostics, and direct management of gateway-backed sections. - Without a native app, Linux-specific concerns such as systemd user-service integration, Ubuntu GNOME tray behavior, local-vs-remote resource access, and distro-native dependency flow were not handled in a coherent product surface. - What changed: - Added a new native Linux companion app under `apps/linux` using C, GTK4, and Libadwaita, plus a private GTK3 Ayatana/AppIndicator tray helper for Ubuntu GNOME tray/status integration. - Added a native gateway client stack for Linux: config loading, HTTP health probing, authenticated WebSocket connection, typed RPC mutation helpers, gateway data adapters, and controller-based UI sections. - Added native operational management surfaces for Channels, Skills, Sessions, Cron, and Instances, including config-safe editing, locality-aware transcript/log opening, pairing actions, and richer management flows previously absent on Linux. - Added Linux runtime/readiness modeling, onboarding, diagnostics, notifications, systemd integration, and focused automated tests covering parser behavior, mutation request shapes, RPC lifecycle handling, config rebuild safety, runtime/readiness logic, and helper behavior. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): - This PR does not add distro packaging artifacts such as `.deb`, `.rpm`, or Snap packages. - This PR does not attempt to solve the Windows side. - This PR does not claim full macOS parity across every desktop capability; it establishes the native Linux companion foundation and a substantial in-app management surface. ## Change Type (select all) - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [x] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [x] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [x] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [x] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [x] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Related #75 - [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable) For bug fixes or regressions, explain why this happened, not just what changed. Otherwise write `N/A`. If the cause is unclear, write `Unknown`. - Root cause: - N/A - Missing detection / guardrail: - N/A - Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): - N/A - Why this regressed now: - N/A - If unknown, what was ruled out: - N/A ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) For bug fixes or regressions, name the smallest reliable test coverage that should have caught this. If none, write `None`. - Linux now has a native GTK4 + Libadwaita companion app in-repo. - Ubuntu GNOME users get tray/status integration through the companion plus the private AppIndicator helper. - The Linux app can discover and work with the user `openclaw-gateway.service` lifecycle through native systemd integration. - The app surfaces first-run progression clearly across the main readiness states: - before `openclaw setup` - after `openclaw setup` but before gateway install - after gateway install with the service active and the gateway answering - The app surfaces runtime/readiness/onboarding/diagnostics states directly in the Linux UI. - Channels can now be inspected and managed in-app, including probe, logout, config editing, and WhatsApp QR linking flow. - Skills can now be filtered and managed in-app, including enable/disable, install, and env/API-key updates. - Sessions can now be managed in-app, including patch/reset/compact/delete and log access. - Cron can now be managed in-app, including scheduler status, recent runs, create/edit, run-now, enable/disable, delete, and transcript access. - Instances now expose richer remote node details, pending pairing approval/reject flows, and copy-debug-info behavior. - Log/transcript opening is locality-aware: local resources open locally when available, otherwise the UI falls back safely. - Channel config editing now validates edited JSON, preserves unrelated config keys, and saves using `baseHash`. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: [user on Linux] -> [CLI / dashboard / partial prototype paths] -> [limited lifecycle visibility and little or no native management] After: [user on Linux] -> [native GTK4 companion app] -> [systemd + HTTP + authenticated WebSocket runtime model] -> [tray / diagnostics / onboarding / management sections] -> [native actions for channels, skills, sessions, cron, instances] ```` ## Security Impact (required) * New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: * The Linux companion introduces a new native desktop surface that can read local runtime context, inspect service state, connect to the local gateway over HTTP/WebSocket, edit config, open local logs/transcripts when available, and trigger gateway-backed management mutations. * Risk is mitigated by keeping the runtime model explicit, separating systemd discovery from gateway RPC transport, validating config JSON before save, preserving unrelated config content during rebuild, using `baseHash` on config writes, hardening request shapes through typed mutation helpers, and covering lifecycle/parsing/request-shape behavior in targeted tests. * Local-vs-remote resource access is handled explicitly so the app does not blindly assume every gateway-returned path is locally openable. ## Repro + Verification ### Environment * OS: * Ubuntu 24.04 and Ubuntu 26.04 GNOME * Runtime/container: * Bare-metal / local user-session workflow with systemd user service * Model/provider: * Local gateway-backed companion flow; model/provider depends on gateway config * Integration/channel (if any): * systemd user service, HTTP health, authenticated gateway WebSocket, GTK4 + Libadwaita, Ayatana/AppIndicator * Relevant config (redacted): * Fresh local OpenClaw config and user `openclaw-gateway.service`; secrets redacted ### Steps 1. Install Linux build dependencies and clone/build OpenClaw. 2. Build and run the Linux app with Meson. 3. Launch the Linux companion app before running `openclaw setup`. 4. Run `openclaw setup`, then relaunch or refresh the companion app. 5. Install and start the user gateway service. 6. Launch or refresh the Linux companion app again. 7. Exercise tray/status, diagnostics, onboarding/readiness, and the Dashboard / General / Channels / Skills / Sessions / Cron / Instances sections. 8. Run the Linux test suite. ### Expected * Before setup, the app reports the missing setup/runtime state clearly. * After setup but before gateway install, the app reports configured-but-not-installed service state clearly. * After gateway install/start, the app reports a healthy connected state, with diagnostics, dashboard, and general surfaces reflecting the running gateway. * The Linux app builds, launches, connects through the native runtime model, reflects systemd/gateway state accurately, and exposes native management flows for the major gateway-backed sections. * The Linux test suite passes. ### Actual * Matches expected in local verification. ## Evidence Attach at least one: * [x] Failing test/log before + passing after * [x] Trace/log snippets * [x] Screenshot/recording * [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What I personally verified (not just CI), and how: * Verified scenarios: * Built the Linux app from a clean checkout on Ubuntu 24.04 and Ubuntu 26.04 GNOME. * Ran the Meson test suite locally. * Verified tray helper spawn and tray/status behavior. * Verified systemd user-service discovery and lifecycle reflection. * Verified diagnostics/readiness/runtime presentation. * Verified first-run progression manually with screenshots: * app launched before `openclaw setup` * app after `openclaw setup` * app after gateway install/start with the gateway answering properly * Verified the healthy connected state manually against a fresh configured local gateway. * Verified additional Linux app surfaces manually, including Dashboard, General, and Diagnostics. * Verified the main Linux companion window and controller-backed sections load and refresh. * Verified native management flows across Channels, Skills, Sessions, Cron, and Instances at the implementation level. * Verified config editing flow behavior, including full-document rebuild and hash-aware save path. * Verified locality-aware log/transcript fallback behavior. * Edge cases checked: * Invalid config JSON aborts save. * Config rebuild preserves unrelated top-level keys and sibling channel config. * Mutation request shapes match the intended backend contract structure. * RPC lifecycle handling covers success/error/timeout/disconnect cleanup paths. * Tray-helper lifecycle and cleanup behavior were tightened. * Readiness states remain intelligible across the bootstrap sequence from no setup -> configured -> installed/running. * What I did **not** verify: * Official distro packaging artifacts (`.deb`, `.rpm`, Snap) are not included here. * Broad desktop-environment compatibility beyond the Ubuntu GNOME target path. * Full end-to-end parity for every macOS companion capability. ## Review Conversations * [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. * [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers. ## Compatibility / Migration * Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) * Yes * Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) * No * Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) * No * If yes, exact upgrade steps: * N/A ## Risks and Mitigations List only real risks for this PR. Add/remove entries as needed. If none, write `None`. * Risk: * Linux desktop behavior can vary by distro and shell, especially around tray hosting. * Mitigation: * Target the initial implementation clearly at Ubuntu GNOME, use a private AppIndicator helper, and keep the helper boundary isolated from the GTK4 main process. * Risk: * The Linux companion now depends on a larger native runtime stack: systemd context, HTTP health, WebSocket RPC, and gateway payload parsing. * Mitigation: * Keep those concerns separated into dedicated modules and cover parser/RPC/mutation behavior with focused tests. * Risk: * Config editing could accidentally overwrite unrelated config content if the save path is too narrow. * Mitigation: * Load the full config document, edit only the relevant subtree, rebuild the full document, validate JSON before save, and send `baseHash` with `config.set`. * Risk: * Transcript/log opening can fail or behave incorrectly if the gateway resource is not local to the GTK host. * Mitigation: * Enforce locality-aware fallback logic and only open local resources directly when they are actually present and accessible. * Risk: * This is a large first-class app addition and therefore a large review surface. * Mitigation: * Keep the app organized into focused subsystems and section controllers, provide a documented Linux build/test path, and include targeted tests for the most contract-sensitive areas.

target.title: refactor: consolidate duplicated plugin state and doctor migration plumbing onto SDK seams
target.body:
Closes #99841

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves the largest verbatim code-duplication clusters in the bundled plugins, where channel and doctor plumbing was copy-pasted per plugin instead of flowing through plugin SDK family seams:

- Slack (x2), Mattermost, and MS Teams each hand-rolled the same dual-layer presence cache (global in-memory dedupe + best-effort persistent keyed store with disable-on-error). Slack and Mattermost were ~95% identical whole files and the top jscpd hit in the repo (40-line verbatim clone).
- Matrix reimplemented the approval-reaction target store that `openclaw/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime` already provides and imessage/signal/whatsapp already use. The local copy had drifted: its in-memory map was unbounded and never expired entries.
- `fileExists` was copied verbatim into 10 extension `doctor-contract-api.ts` files and `archiveLegacySource` into 9, with per-plugin label prefixes baked into otherwise identical doctor message templates.
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-runtime-cache.ts` validated the same cache-entry envelope twice in two 50-line normalizers.

Every copy was a drift bug waiting to happen; `extensions/AGENTS.md` explicitly calls this out ("stop copying the logic. Extract one shared helper and migrate both call sites in the same change").

## Why This Change Was Made

One canonical owner per behavior, per the repo architecture rules:

- New `createPersistentDedupeCache` family helper in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime` (memory-first presence checks, best-effort persistence that disables itself on the first state failure so message handling never breaks, re-prime on persistent hits). The four presence-cache files shrink to thin key-shape wrappers; persisted record shapes and namespaces are unchanged, so no state migration is needed.
- Matrix now builds on `createApprovalReactionTargetStore` like its sibling channels, keeping only the matrix-specific emoji bindings local (checkmark/cross render reliably across Matrix clients). The persisted `{version: 1, target}` wire format is unchanged and asserted by existing tests. The test-only sync resolver export was dropped; production callers always used the persistence-aware resolver.
- `legacyStateFileExists` / `archiveLegacyStateSource` are now exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-doctor` (implementation in `src/plugins/doctor-state-migration-fs.ts`, next to the doctor contract registry) and all ten doctor contracts consume them. Doctor change/warning strings are preserved via the label parameter (asserted by the existing doctor-contract tests).

Reviewed and intentionally left as-is, with reasons: the msteams-local `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` copy (documented hot-path load-cost tradeoff vs the broad `media-runtime` barrel), the discord components-registry store wrapper (linked two-store disable + richer error formatting = different contract), and the core-side OpenAI OAuth TLS preflight twin (`src/plugins/provider-openai-chatgpt-oauth-tls.ts`), which needs a doctor-contract ownership decision tracked in #99841.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Channel presence caches, approval reactions, and doctor migrations behave as before; two internal hardening side effects: the Matrix approval-reaction memory layer is now bounded/TTL-pruned like its siblings, and the MS Teams sent-message memory layer moves from unbounded per-conversation maps to one globally bounded dedupe cache (20k entries). Net -539 lines of production/test code.

## Evidence

- `git diff --numstat` vs base: 380 added / 919 deleted (net -539).
- Verbatim-clone proof: targeted jscpd re-scan (min 15 lines / 120 tokens) over all touched packages reports 0 clones involving the refactored files (was: 40L slack<->mattermost, 32L qmd self-clone, 24L active-memory<->nostr, 18L matrix cluster).
- Repo gates: `node scripts/check-duplicates.mjs` (production/tests/src-mixed all 0 clones), `check-architecture-smells.mjs`, `check-database-first-legacy-stores.mjs`, `check-no-extension-src-imports.ts`, `check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mjs`, `check-plugin-extension-import-boundary.mjs`, `check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs`, `check-import-cycles.ts` - all clean.
- Types: all four tsgo lanes clean (core, extensions, core-test, extensions-test).
- Build: `node scripts/build-all.mjs` green, including the `check-plugin-sdk-exports` gate.
- Tests (node scripts/run-vitest.mjs): new `src/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime.test.ts` (6 tests: layering, re-prime timestamps, disable-on-error, test reset); existing suites for all migrated files pass unchanged except for three matrix test files updated to the async resolver and one memory-wiki doctor wording assertion ("legacy record" -> canonical "legacy source"): slack sent-thread/inbound-delivery + send/upload/blocks/message-handler + dispatch.streaming (13+50+26), mattermost thread-participation + monitor-gating (5 incl. persisted-shape assertions, +17 shard), msteams sent-message-cache + thread-parent/thread-session handlers (4+7+17 shard), matrix approval-reactions/handler/reaction-events (14+7), all 10 doctor-contract suites, memory-core qmd-runtime-cache (10), plugin-sdk subpath contracts (18) and api-baseline (3).
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.5, full bundle): "patch is correct (0.82) - No actionable defects found. The shared persistent dedupe helper preserves the existing memory-first behavior, handles persistence failures as best-effort, and the migrated call sites keep their prior TTL and fallback semantics."

target.title: fix(android): block loopback canvas navigation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an Android canvas navigation gap where a gateway-controlled `canvas.navigate` URL could load loopback services on the Android device, including through WebView-compatible URL forms or main-frame redirects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Android now normalizes canvas navigation targets before loading them and falls back to the bundled canvas for loopback or malformed `http(s)` targets whose host cannot be safely extracted. The Canvas WebViewClient applies the same check to main-frame navigations and redirects so remote pages cannot redirect the canvas into device-local services.

## User Impact

Android users keep normal remote canvas pages and bundled file canvases, while local-device loopback services are no longer reachable through the canvas surface. This does not add settings, migrations, release-flow changes, or provider behavior changes.

target.title: fix(gateway): clear model discovery cache during hot reload to prevent stale registries

## What Problem This Solves

Config hot reload drops include-defined models (`OPENCLAW_INCLUDE_ROOTS`) from the running gateway's in-memory model registry, causing phantom `FailoverError: Unknown model: <id>` until a full restart.
- **Problem**: `resetPreparedModelRuntimeStateForHotReload()` clears the model catalog cache, provider auth state, and gateway model catalog staleness — but NOT the per-agent `DISCOVERY_STORE_CACHE`. After a hot reload where the resolved config snapshot (with includes correctly merged) is rebuilt, cached per-agent registries remain stale.
- **Solution**: Add `resetModelDiscoveryCache()` to the existing hot-reload model-state reset path. The cache is lazily repopulated on the next embedded-agent turn — negligible cost given hot reloads are infrequent relative to agent calls.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-discovery-cache.ts` (renamed `resetModelDiscoveryCacheForTest` → `resetModelDiscoveryCache`, added deprecated alias) + `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts` (import + call in `resetPreparedModelRuntimeStateForHotReload`).
- **What did NOT change**: Cache fingerprint logic, agent model discovery pipeline, config include resolution, any provider-specific code.

- [ ] API / contracts

The on-disk config remains valid (`openclaw models list` resolves all models correctly), but the running gateway rejects include-defined models until restarted. The `discoveryFingerprint()` function in `model-discovery-cache.ts:75-94` builds a cache key from file metadata only (agent dir, sqlite mtime/size, models.json mtime, plugin catalog files). It does not include a fingerprint of the resolved config's `models.providers`. - `discoveryFingerprint`: introduced by Vincent Koc on 2026-06-17 (`1ee2733b2f`)
- `resetPreparedModelRuntimeStateForHotReload`: carried forward from the same refactor
- Made visible by: users running `OPENCLAW_INCLUDE_ROOTS` with hot-reload-active gateways
- Confidence: **clear**

## Regression Test Plan

Updated event-order assertion validates that `resetPreparedModelRuntimeStateForHotReload()` fires `reset-model-discovery-cache` alongside `reset-model-catalog` and `clear-provider-auth` in the correct lifecycle order (both before and after plugin reload).

- **Best fix**: Yes. The per-agent discovery cache invalidation during the existing hot-reload model-state reset is the narrowest owner-boundary fix — it mirrors the existing `resetModelCatalogCache()` call that already runs in the same function.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding config fingerprint to `discoveryFingerprint()`. Rejected because the cache is designed for file-backed stability; adding config content would couple a filesystem cache to runtime config state, and hot reload is infrequent enough that simple invalidation is cheaper than fingerprint tracking.

- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- [x] Data access scope changed? No

target.title: fix(auto-reply): stop rendering misleading /compact labels on small sessions
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: Running \`/compact\` on a session with little or no summarizable history can render labels like \`Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\` — the arrow direction is reversed, and the denominator context number is wrong.
- **Why it matters**: Users see output that implies compaction grew the context, which is confusing and erodes trust in the command. The 0%/36-token display also misrepresents actual session size.
- **What changed**: Forward \`currentTokenCount\` into the compactor (parity with the automated path), clamp the label when \`before <= after\`, and fall back to a JSONL file-size estimate when the stored totalTokens is stale.
- **What did NOT change**: No API/contract changes, no schema changes. Pure UX + one new optional forward.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] UI / DX
- [x] Integrations (messaging reply formatting — Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord all consume this line)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Three related issues in \`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts\`:

1. \`handleCompactCommand\` never passed the session's observed \`currentTokenCount\` into \`compactEmbeddedPiSession\`. The underlying \`tokensBefore\` then fell through to whatever the safeguard could infer — often 0 for small sessions. The automated/preflight compaction path in \`agent-runner-memory.ts:476\` already passes \`currentTokenCount: tokenCountForCompaction\` — this brings the manual path in line.

2. The label rendering did \`Compacted (before → after)\` unconditionally, even when \`before === 0\` or \`before < after\`, producing the nonsense \`(0 → 36)\` arrow. Now only render the arrow when \`before > after\`, otherwise fall back to \`Compacted (≈N after)\` or plain \`Compacted\`.

3. The post-compaction context summary used \`resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens()\` alone. For backends/cases where \`totalTokens\` is stale — e.g. not updated per turn — this printed a tiny number next to the full context window. Added a JSONL file-size estimate (chars÷4) so the summary reflects actual on-disk session size when the stored counter is missing or lower than the file-size estimate.

## Evidence

- [x] Repro: on a Telegram session with 14 JSONL entries and stale \`totalTokens: 36\`, \`/compact\` rendered \`⚙️ Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\`. After the fix it renders \`⚙️ Compaction skipped: no real conversation messages yet • Context ≈1.7k/1.0m (0%)\`.
- [x] Existing test suite in \`commands-compact.test.ts\` still passes (7/7). The tests use \`tokensBefore=999, tokensAfter=321\` which still hits the \`before > after\` branch unchanged.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
  - Skipped compaction on a small Telegram session — no more \`(0 → 36)\` arrow.
  - Happy-path compaction with known token counts — arrow still renders.
  - Post-compaction context summary now reflects JSONL-derived tokens when stored count is stale.
- Edge cases checked:
  - Missing session file (stat throws) — estimator returns \`undefined\`, falls back to the stored value.
  - Empty file — estimator skips via the \`size > 0\` guard.
  - \`before === after\` — renders \`Compacted (≈N after)\` instead of \`(N → N)\`.
- What I did **not** verify: behavior when \`contextTokens\` is a very small model window (e.g. 8k). Math should still hold but I only tested with 200k/1M windows.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: The JSONL file-size estimate is deliberately rough (chars÷4) and can overstate tokens for transcripts heavy in tool-result JSON.
  - Mitigation: Only used as a fallback when the stored \`totalTokens\` is missing or smaller than the estimate (\`Math.max\`). If the stored number is fresh and larger, it wins. The UI label prefix \`≈\` also signals it's approximate.

The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.

target.title: fix(edit): keep mismatch hint truncation unicode-safe
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the edit-tool mismatch diagnostic truncation path so the `Current file contents:` hint cannot split an emoji or other astral Unicode character at the 800-character cutoff.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** When an edit replacement cannot find its exact `oldText`, the diagnostic should show trustworthy current-file context. A broken replacement character at the truncation boundary makes the hint harder to use when the file contains non-BMP Unicode near the cutoff.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this focused diagnostic fix. The patch touches only the edit-tool mismatch hint path and is covered by a live edit-tool invocation, a targeted regression test, and changed-file core checks.
- **What did NOT change:** Edit matching, replacement semantics, file writes, newline normalization, post-write recovery, preview rendering, approval flows, gateway protocol, UI approval surfaces, generated Swift models, and plugin/native channel behavior are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Edit-tool exact-match failures append `Current file contents:` to the thrown mismatch error. Before this change, long current-file snippets were truncated with raw `String.prototype.slice(0, 800)`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair when the cutoff lands inside an emoji or other astral Unicode character.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 via Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From the repository root, I ran a non-test live edit-tool invocation with `node --import tsx`. The script imported `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts`, created a temporary file containing 799 ASCII characters, one `🙂` emoji, and trailing text, then called `createEditTool(...).execute(...)` with a missing `oldText` to trigger the real mismatch diagnostic path. I also ran the focused regression test and changed-file checks:

```text
node --import tsx <live edit-tool invocation script>
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts
git diff --check
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The live edit-tool invocation produced this copied terminal output, with the temp path redacted:

```text
temp file: <temp-dir>\unicode-boundary.txt
message includes exact mismatch header: true
message includes intact emoji at boundary: true
message includes replacement character: false
snippet tail:
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa🙂
... (truncated)

LIVE_PROOF_EXIT:0
```

The focused edit-tool test suite exited 0. `git diff --check` exited 0. The local changed-file check exited 0 and selected the core/core-test lanes for `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts` and `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The live mismatch diagnostic includes the exact mismatch header, keeps the full boundary emoji before `... (truncated)`, and does not contain the Unicode replacement character. The regression test verifies the same boundary case through `createEditTool(...).execute(...)`, so the hint no longer relies on raw `.slice()` truncation at the UTF-16 boundary.
- **What was not tested:** No live external channel, Telegram, Matrix, iMessage, Control UI, gateway, Mantis, or Desktop proof was run because the current patch does not touch those paths. A plain `pnpm check:changed` invocation attempted to delegate to Blacksmith Testbox through `crabbox`, but this host's `crabbox` binary failed its basic sanity check before running repo checks. The local child-mode command above was used for the actual changed-file verification.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## What Problem This Solves

When an edit replacement cannot find its exact `oldText`, the edit tool appends `Current file contents:` to help the model/user see what actually exists in the file. For long files this diagnostic is capped at `EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT` characters.

Before this change, the cap used raw JavaScript string slicing. JavaScript `slice()` counts UTF-16 code units, not displayed Unicode characters/code points. If an emoji or other astral character straddled the 800-code-unit boundary, the hint could include only half of the surrogate pair. That produces a malformed diagnostic snippet at the exact point where the tool is trying to provide useful mismatch context.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The edit mismatch diagnostic source of truth is `appendMismatchHint()`, and that formatter truncated `currentContent` with `currentContent.slice(0, EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT)`. That operation counts UTF-16 code units instead of whole Unicode code points, so the diagnostic owner could create an invalid snippet by cutting between the high and low surrogate of a non-BMP character.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix changes the truncation primitive at the diagnostic source of truth, before the mismatch hint string is assembled. Iterating with `for...of` makes the formatter count whole Unicode code points, so the invariant becomes: the edit mismatch hint may be shortened, but it never creates a malformed half-character at the truncation boundary. This fixes the source formatter rather than masking replacement characters after the fact.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth boundary is the private edit-tool mismatch hint formatter in `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts`. No public contract, schema, protocol, config, generated model, or API surface is changed; compatibility and default behavior for edit execution are unchanged. A related open PR / same-contract scan is not relevant because this patch does not define or expand a public contract surface. Out of scope: changing edit matching, replacement, persistence, preview rendering, gateway behavior, approval UI, or any protocol field.

## Changes

- Added a small edit-tool-local mismatch snippet helper that iterates `currentContent` with `for...of`, so the cutoff is counted by Unicode code point instead of raw UTF-16 code unit.
- Preserved the existing mismatch hint limit and `... (truncated)` suffix behavior.
- Added a regression test where the 800th displayed character is an emoji, proving the hint keeps the emoji intact before appending the truncation marker.

## Review findings addressed from the previous PR content

This PR previously carried a different approval-prompt/protocol/UI change. That old diff has been removed from the branch and replaced with the focused edit-tool fix above.

- RF-001 / RF-002 / RF-004 / RF-006: old requests for real Telegram, Control UI, gateway, or approval prompt proof no longer apply to the current diff because the approval-flow changes were removed.
- RF-003: old public-ish approval contract compatibility concern no longer applies; the current diff does not touch gateway protocol, generated Swift models, plugin SDK reply parameters, or approval metadata.
- RF-005: the previous draft/readiness gate was for the old approval PR content. Current readiness should be judged from the new edit-tool diff and verification below.
- RF-007: old UI i18n concern no longer applies; the current diff does not add or change approval UI warnings.

## Evidence

The live proof and regression test both covered the real edit-tool mismatch error path through `createEditTool(...).execute(...)`, not only a standalone helper. The boundary file contains 799 ASCII characters followed by an emoji and trailing text, then triggers an exact-match miss. The observed diagnostic includes the intact emoji and the existing truncation marker.

Changed-file verification also covered:

```text
conflict markers
changelog attributions
guarded extension wildcard re-exports
plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports
duplicate scan target coverage
dependency pin guard
package patch guard
test temp creation report
typecheck core
typecheck core tests
lint core changed files
database-first legacy-store guard
media download helper guard
runtime sidecar loader guard
runtime import cycles
webhook body guard
pairing store guard
pairing account guard
```

All selected local changed-file lanes exited 0.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A mismatch hint whose truncation boundary lands after 799 ASCII characters and one emoji.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test exercises the public edit-tool execution path, so it verifies the actual error message users/models see without exporting a formatting helper or adding broader fixtures.
- Expected behavior: the thrown mismatch error contains the full emoji followed by `... (truncated)`, not a sliced surrogate half or replacement character.
- Existing mismatch behavior remains covered by the existing exact-match diagnostic test.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** No `merge-risk:*` label should be required for the current diff. The old approval-protocol/UI compatibility risk no longer applies because that diff was removed.
- **Risk explanation:** The change is isolated to diagnostic formatting for edit-tool mismatch errors and keeps the same limit/suffix contract. It does not change edit application, matching, persistence, protocol, UI, or approval behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** Counting the truncation limit by Unicode code point prevents malformed diagnostics while preserving bounded output and the existing truncation marker. The only behavior difference is that astral Unicode characters are kept whole at the boundary.
- **Patch quality notes:** This is not a fallback or downstream string special-case. It fixes the truncation primitive at the mismatch hint source, keeps the helper private to the edit tool, and adds a regression test for the exact boundary failure mode.

target.title: fix(subagents): killed subagent runs stay running in the task list
target.body:
Related: #90444

**Prompt request:** Make every path that kills a subagent run finalize its detached task-registry row, so the task list reflects the kill instead of showing the task as running forever, while leaving the kill and abort behavior itself unchanged.

**Proof target:** Show that after a `subagents` kill the killed run's task row flips to `cancelled`, while normal completion and failure transitions go through unchanged code paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who kill a running subagent (via the `subagents` kill tool, its kill-all and cascade variants, or by aborting the parent reply) keep seeing that task as `running` in `openclaw tasks list` indefinitely. The in-memory subagent registry records the kill and the chat reply says the run was killed, but the detached task-registry row is never finalized, so task surfaces disagree with what actually happened and the phantom `running` entry never clears.

## Why This Change Was Made

`markSubagentRunTerminated` sets `endedAt` synchronously, which short-circuits the completion watcher — the lifecycle finalizer that normally updates the task row never runs for killed runs, and no kill caller finalized the ledger itself. This change finalizes the task row as `cancelled` inside `markSubagentRunTerminated`, the termination primitive all kill paths funnel through (tool kill and its kill-all and cascade variants, admin kill, and the parent-reply abort path in `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts`). Already-ended entries are skipped so the finalize stays single-shot, and a finalize failure degrades to a warning without breaking termination. The operator `tasks cancel` path keeps its own status update, which now becomes an idempotent overwrite of the same state. The existing late-completion recovery stays authoritative: when a COMPLETE lands after a kill marker and the lifecycle un-kills and announces the run, the run-scoped guard now lets that completion upgrade the row from `cancelled` to `succeeded` for subagent tasks, so the task list matches the announced outcome. Late failures and other runtimes keep sticky `cancelled`. This PR covers the direct kill-path write at the shared termination primitive; reconciliation of rows that are already stuck is separate work.

## User Impact

`openclaw tasks list` and task status surfaces now show killed subagent runs as `cancelled` (with a short reason) instead of a permanently `running` phantom entry. Successful, failed, and timed-out runs keep their existing transitions — those code paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture driving the production path with no mocks at any layer — real `registerSubagentRun`, real `subagents` kill, and `listTaskRecords` reading real registry rows from an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (a hanging gateway socket keeps the completion watcher pending, as it is while a real child run executes):

Before (main):

```
[after-spawn] taskId=65238e57-8192-4f19-bb8a-76ecf8c3d4ff runtime=subagent status=running error=-
[kill] status=ok text=killed proof task: long-running background work.
[after-kill] taskId=65238e57-8192-4f19-bb8a-76ecf8c3d4ff runtime=subagent status=running error=-
```

After (this PR):

```
[after-spawn] taskId=a06f3326-23f8-4900-a0a8-73251b0234ca runtime=subagent status=running error=-
[kill] status=ok text=killed proof task: long-running background work.
[after-kill] taskId=a06f3326-23f8-4900-a0a8-73251b0234ca runtime=subagent status=cancelled error=Subagent run killed.
```

Focused tests: `src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts` (90 passed) — an authoritative late completion upgrades a cancelled subagent row to `succeeded`, while late failures and non-subagent runtimes keep sticky `cancelled`. `src/agents/subagent-control.test.ts` (30 passed) — a tool kill finalizes the row as `cancelled`, a rejected kill leaves the ledger untouched, a throwing finalize still reports the kill, and the admin kill path finalizes the same way; the two ledger assertions fail without the fix. The kill-all and cascade variants are covered through the shared primitive. `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.test.ts` (31 passed) covers the parent-reply abort caller reaching the same termination primitive.

target.title: fix(compaction): ensure per-call usage total is populated before compaction estimation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99843 — Auto-compaction can fire far below the configured trigger when `calculateContextTokens` falls back to summing `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` with **turn-aggregated** cache fields. The root cause is in `recordAssistantUsage`: when the provider stream event does not carry a `total` token count, `pendingUsage.total` stays undefined. Downstream, `preservePendingAssistantUsage` falls back to summing the component fields, which can carry accumulated `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` from multiple API calls in a single tool-loop turn (~12 calls × ~150k cached tokens = 819k+ aggregated), producing a ~5.7x inflated context estimate.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause fix** (`recordAssistantUsage`): Populate `usage.total` from per-call component fields when the provider omits it, so downstream always has a correct per-call total. This prevents the turn-aggregated fallback path from engaging.

**Defense-in-depth** (`calculateContextTokens`): The fallback formula `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` is correct for single-call usage and properly accounts for cached prompt context (unlike `input + output` alone which would undercount). With the root cause fixed, the fallback is safe.

## User Impact

- Sessions doing long multi-call turns (agentic tool loops with prompt caching) will no longer compact prematurely due to inflated estimates
- Single-call cached sessions with missing `totalTokens` will still get correct context estimates (cache fields are included in the fallback)
- The compaction banner will display accurate token estimates

## Evidence

- **Root cause identified**: `recordAssistantUsage` → `preservePendingAssistantUsage` chain in `embedded-agent-subscribe.ts`
- **Source-level fix**: 3 lines added in `recordAssistantUsage` + updated JSDoc in `calculateContextTokens`
- **Tests added**: 5 tests for `calculateContextTokens` covering `totalTokens` priority, cached single-call fallback, and edge cases
- **Test results**: `packages/agent-core` compaction tests (6 passed), `src/agents` compaction tests (17 passed), subscribe handler tests (43 passed), additional subscribe tests (2 passed)
- **No existing test regression**

Android node invoke handlers use `parseJsonBooleanFlag` for flags such as `includeSystem`, `includeAudio`, and presence beacon `ok`/`handled`. target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(feishu): upgrade single newlines to paragraph breaks in post md messages
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When OpenClaw sends messages to Feishu via `msg_type: post` with `tag: md`, single newline characters (`\n`) are rendered as plain spaces by the Feishu IM API. This causes multi-paragraph prose to appear visually cramped. Fixes #97074 ## Why This Change Was Made Added `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines()` — a dedicated function that upgrades single `\n` to `\n\n` outside code regions for Feishu post+md rendering. It runs only after the render mode is known, so card and document-comment text are never modified. **Revision 6** (per ClawSweeper re-review — table conversion ordering): 1. **[P2] Convert tables before normalization in outbound post path** — `sendOutboundText` now resolves the table mode and runs `convertMarkdownTables` before `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines`. Normalization was inserting blank lines between table rows, which broke table row contiguity for the converter. Converting first preserves table structure for raw-mode Feishu accounts. `sendMessageFeishu` runs `convertMarkdownTables` again internally, but that is a no-op on already-converted text. This matches the `reply-dispatcher` `sendChunkedTextReply` path which already converted tables before normalization. **Revision 5** (per ClawSweeper re-review — single-pass normalization): 2. **[P2] Single-pass normalization for pre-chunked text** — Added `alreadyNormalized` flag to `buildFeishuPostMessagePayload` and `sendMessageFeishu`. Callers that already normalized the full text before chunking pass `alreadyNormalized: true` so the payload builder skips `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines`. This prevents the second normalization pass from expanding code-block newlines when a chunk boundary falls inside a fenced region. 3. **[P2] Reply fanout for expanded subchunks** — Only the first subchunk carries the reply target. Later subchunks send without reply metadata so single-use implicit reply ids are consumed once per platform send. **Revision 4** (ClawSweeper review — three findings addressed): 4. **[P1] Card routing on raw text** — `sendOutboundText` routes `shouldUseCard(text)` on the original text before any normalization. 5. **[P2] Post-md rechunk after expansion** — After normalization, if text exceeds 4000 chars, `sendOutboundText` rechunks and sends each chunk as a separate post message. 6. **[P2] Edit-path length guard** — `editMessageFeishu` checks normalized length against the 4000-char limit before building the payload. ## User Impact - Post-md messages render with visible paragraph breaks instead of cramped single-spaced text - Card-mode and document-comment text is never modified - Single-pass normalization: pre-chunked subchunks are not re-normalized, code-block content split across chunk boundaries is preserved - Markdown tables are converted before normalization, preserving table rendering for raw-mode accounts - Reply fanout preserved: only the first expanded subchunk carries the reply target - Edit path rejects over-limit expanded content with a clear error ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` — 164/164 passed - `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts` — clean - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts` — clean - `pnpm build` — exit 0 (previous run) ### Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: card routing on raw text, post-md rechunk after expansion, edit-path length guard, reply fanout for subchunks, single-pass normalization for pre-chunked text, table conversion before normalization. Real environment tested: Linux (Node 24.13.1), branch `fix/97074-feishu-post-md-newline`, commit `799ca5277f`. Exact steps run: 1. Unit test suite (164 tests): includes `alreadyNormalized` flag tests, split-code-block regression, and table conversion ordering 2. Previous revision: Gateway started — Feishu WebSocket connected, direct API comparison of single-`\n` vs double-`\n` post-md messages **Screenshots**: comparison of single-`\n` vs double-`\n` post-md messages in Feishu client What was not tested: bot reply via gateway (Feishu error 230101 blocked DM replies), older Feishu client versions, live rechunk path, live edit-path limit rejection.

target.title: fix(memory): keep local embedding worker forks working after Homebrew Node upgrades
target.body:
Closes #99183

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the Gateway with Homebrew-managed Node could lose fresh local embedding worker forks after Homebrew upgrades Node and removes the old Cellar binary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local embedding worker now resolves Homebrew Cellar `process.execPath` values to stable Homebrew symlinks before calling `fork()`. Non-Cellar paths keep the existing executable unchanged, and the change stays inside the memory host worker supervisor without adding config, public API, or a new worker error code.

## User Impact

Local semantic-memory embeddings can continue starting fresh worker processes after a Homebrew Node upgrade instead of failing with `spawn ... ENOENT` until the Gateway is restarted.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: stale Homebrew Cellar worker forks use a stable Node executable path before `fork()`, while non-Cellar paths remain unchanged.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stale-execpath.test.ts` -> passed, 4 tests.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts` -> passed, 18 tests.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` -> passed.
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` -> worker reported clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
  - Real macOS/Homebrew proof: https://github.com/qingminglong/openclaw/actions/runs/28698715497 -> passed on `macos-15-arm64`, artifact `pr-99541-macos-homebrew-proof`.
- Observed result:
  - Unit tests verify Cellar paths are passed to `fork()` as `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` or `/usr/local/bin/node`, non-Cellar paths pass through unchanged, and aborts during the new async boundary do not send cancelled requests.
  - The macOS proof ran on macOS 15.7.7 arm64 with Homebrew prefix `/opt/homebrew` and Homebrew Node 26.4.0.
  - The parent process started from a Homebrew Cellar Node executable: `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/openclaw-proof-99541-28698715497-1/bin/node`.
  - After that Cellar executable was removed, a raw `child_process.fork()` without explicit `execPath` failed with `spawn /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/openclaw-proof-99541-28698715497-1/bin/node ENOENT`.
  - The PR worker path then completed successfully while the stale Cellar executable remained unavailable; the child process ran through the stable Homebrew Node path, with child `argv0` recorded as `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` and child `execPath` resolving to `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.4.0/bin/node`.
